【turn874792960view1】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Content type: application/pdf; Number of pages: 2; Source: open({"ref_id":"https://vetmed.illinois.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Canine-Osteosarcoma-pulmonary-metastases.pdf","lineno":null}); Total lines: 49
L0@P0: Patient Disease: Osteosarcoma with pulmonary metastatic disease in dogs
L1@P0: Study Title: Treating osteosarcoma lung lesions with intravenous small molecule
L2@P0: immunotherapy
L3@P0: Purpose of Study/Background/Objectives: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common
L4@P0: primary bone tumor diagnosed in large and giant breed dogs. Conventional therapies for OS
L5@P0: include surgical amputation of the affected site/limb followed by chemotherapy. Despite the use
L6@P0: of systemic treatments, most dogs will have disease spread to the lungs (pulmonary
L7@P0: metastases). Once OS lung lesions develop, treatments are not very effective. As such, there is
L8@P0: a great and unmet clinical need for the discovery of novel treatment strategies that are more
L9@P0: effective for managing OS lung lesions. Evidence supports OS to be a tumor that might respond
L10@P0: to immunotherapy and improve long-term outcomes for patients at various stages of disease.
L11@P0: Inclusion Criteria:
L12@P0: • Historical or active diagnosis of osteosarcoma (any primary site) diagnosed via
L13@P0: histopathology or cytology
L14@P0: • If not previously amputated, primary tumor pain must be controlled
L15@P0: • Nodules must be at least 5mm in diameter on CT scan
L16@P0: • Must be in good overall condition, no other serious uncontrolled illness and have an
L17@P0: expected survival time of at least 9 weeks.
L18@P0: • Must not have had radiation within 1 week or chemotherapy/immunotherapy within 3 weeks.
L19@P0: • Concurrent use of immunosuppressive drugs is not allowed (cyclosporine, Apoquel,
L20@P0: immunosuppressive doses of steroids)
L21@P0: Exclusion Criteria:
L22@P0: • Pleural effusion
L23@P0: • Hypoxia or signs of respiratory distress
L24@P0: Eligibility Diagnostics:
L25@P0: • CBC/Chem/Urinalysis
L26@P0: • Thoracic radiographs
L27@P0: • Abdominal ultrasound
L28@P0: Treatment/Protocol: The patient will receive up to 8 IV doses of Z-007 once weekly. During
L29@P0: treatment (treatment #1, #4 and #8) patients will be required to stay in hospital or return the next
L30@P0: day for a blood draw. Patients will receive a thoracic computed tomography (CT) scan at the
L31@P0: first visit along with complete bloodwork at every visit. Patients will return to the hospital 1 week
L32@P0: after their last treatment for a recheck CT scan. If there is an objective response (shrinkage of
L33@P0-1: pulmonary nodules by greater than 30%) at week 9, continued compassionate use of Z-007 might be offered at the discretion of the attending clinician(s), otherwise the patient is off trial
L34@P1: and will be offered other options.
L35@P1: Owner Responsibilities:
L36@P1: • You are responsible for the initial exam and diagnostics to determine eligibility
L37@P1: • You are expected to make and keep all appointments associated with the study
L38@P1: • You are responsible for all costs associated with unrelated medical conditions
L39@P1: Compensation: This is a fully funded trial. Owners are responsible for all charges to deem
L40@P1: their pet eligible for the clinical trial. After eligibility the clinical trial will cover the cost of exam
L41@P1: fees, bloodwork, Z-007 administration and CT’s.
L42@P1: Contact Us: Our trials team will need to have an appointment with both the owner and pet to
L43@P1: assess eligibility. To make an appointment please call 217-333-5300.
L44@P1: They will also need records from your veterinarian. After the appointment has been made the
L45@P1: records can be emailed to medrec@illinois.edu or faxed to 217-244-2554.
L46@P1: If you have further questions please feel free to contact our Clinical Trials Coordinator, Rebecca
L47@P1: Kamerer, at (217) 300-6453 or rmoss81@illinois.edu
L48@P1: Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.

L0@P0: Patient Disease: Treatment of canine multicentric lymphoma
L1@P0: Study Title: Assessing the efficacy and tolerability of daunomustine in dogs with multicentric
L2@P0: lymphoma.
L3@P0: Purpose of Study/Background/Objectives: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the
L4@P0: efficacy of a novel chemotherapy drug, daunomustine, in treatment naïve dogs with multicentric
L5@P0: lymphoma.
L6@P0: Inclusion Criteria:
L7@P0: • Cytologic or histologic diagnosis of multicentric lymphoma from a peripheral node
L8@P0: • Treatment naïve including steroids
L9@P0: • Adequate organ function
L10@P0: • Favorable performance status
L11@P0: Exclusion Criteria:
L12@P0: • Dogs weighing < 4 kgs or that are < 1 yr of age
L13@P0: • Indolent or small cell lymphoma
L14@P0: • Previous chemotherapy or steroid therapy (use of steroid-containing topicals allowed)
L15@P0: • Liver values > 4x normal or elevated total bilirubin
L16@P0: • BUN and Creatinine > 1.5x normal. Minerals (excluding calcium), electrolytes, and
L17@P0: albumin within 20% of the margins of normal range. Hypercalcemic dogs can enroll if
L18@P0: they feel well and are otherwise eligible.
L19@P0: • Thrombocytopenia < 100,000, Neutropenia < 2,000
L20@P0: • Dilated cardiomyopathy (left ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction) or history of
L21@P0: congestive heart failure
L22@P0: Eligibility Diagnostics:
L23@P0: • CBC, Chemistry Panel, U/A
L24@P0: • Cytology or histopathologic diagnosis of lymphoma
L25@P0: Treatment/Protocol: The patient will receive up to 5 doses of IV daunomustine given every 14
L26@P0: days. At each treatment, dose will be escalated within the patient based on response. Patients
L27@P0: will return to the U of I seven days after each treatment for bloodwork and exam as deem
L28@P0: necessary. Following completion of the 5 doses the patient will return every 2 weeks for 2 visits,
L29@P0: then every 2 months for 2 visits, then every 3 months long term, where exam and lab work will
L30@P0: be performed. A single dose of l-asparaginase will be given as deemed appropriate during the
L31@P0: protocol for patients not in complete remission. Patients will be treated on an outpatient basis
L32@P0: and go home each day. Patients will be removed from trial and offered standard of care if they
L33@P0-1: are assessed as having progressive disease.Owner Commitments: Owner Commitments:
L34@P1: • Pet owners are responsible for the initial exam and diagnostics to determine eligibility
L35@P1: • Pet owners are expected to make and keep all appointments associated with the study
L36@P1: • Pet owners are responsible for all costs associated with unrelated medical conditions
L37@P1: Compensation:
L38@P1: • This is a fully funded trial once the pet is deemed eligible
L39@P1: • In the event of adverse events, partial funding to cover these costs is available if
L40@P1: treatment is pursued at the University of Illinois.
L41@P1: • After completion of trial participation (or removal from trial due to stable or progressive
L42@P1: disease) a $1,000 incentive to be used at the U of I VTH will be awarded.
L43@P1: Contact Us: Our trials team recommends scheduling an on-site appointment to assess the
L44@P1: pet’s eligibility. We do not require a referral. The professional fee for the consultation is
L45@P1: approximately $250 and does not include tests, medications or treatments that may be
L46@P1: recommended at the appointment. To schedule please call 217-333-5300.
L47@P1: We would like the opportunity to review the pet’s records from the veterinarian. After the
L48@P1: appointment has been made the records can be emailed to medrec@illinois.edu or faxed to
L49@P1: 217-244-2554.
L50@P1: If you have further questions, please contact our Clinical Trials Coordinator, Rebecca Kamerer,
L51@P1: at (217) 300-6453 or rmoss81@illinois.edu
L52@P1: Referring veterinarians and client calls are welcome.
L53@P1: Please check our up-to-date website to see if this trial is still active and enrolling.
L54@P1: https://vetmed.illinois.edu/research/clinical-trials/

L2: ENROLLING SOON
L3: # A clinical study for dogs with hemangiosarcoma
L4: 
L5: If your dog has recently been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, our clinical study at the University of Illinois Veterinary Hospital in Urbana may be an option, and there is no cost to take part. The study is testing FAM-010, a new investigational chemotherapy designed to be gentler on the heart. Your dog may be eligible if they recently had their spleen removed or have surgery scheduled.
L6: 
L7: [Button: Contact the study team]
L8: 【1†Image: A calm dog resting its head on a bed while a person gently pets it.】
L9: ## What is hemangiosarcoma?
L10: 
L11: Hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that starts in the blood vessels, most often in the spleen. It often shows few signs until a tumor bleeds, so many dogs are diagnosed suddenly, sometimes in an emergency.
L12: 
L13: Treatment usually starts with surgery to remove the spleen, followed by chemotherapy. Even with both, the cancer often comes back, and there is still no FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs.
L14: ## How is FAM-010 different?
L15: 
L16: Doxorubicin is the current standard chemotherapy for dogs with hemangiosarcoma after surgery. But it can also reach and damage healthy tissues, especially the heart. This limits the total amount of chemotherapy a dog can receive.
L17: 
L18: FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin, designed to carry more of the medicine to the cancer and less of it to the heart. We hope this will let dogs receive more of the treatment they need, more safely.
L19: ## What will this study tell us?
L20: 
L21: This first study will find the right dose of FAM-010 for dogs: the highest dose they can receive without side effects becoming too much. Every dog in the study receives FAM-010, given as a short infusion every three weeks at the University of Illinois, and the study team monitors each dog closely throughout.
L22: 
L23: FAM-010 is investigational and not approved by FDA for dogs. This study is designed to establish the dose and understand its side effects.
L24: 
L25: STUDY ELIGIBILITY
L26: ## Could this study be an option for your dog?
L27: 
L28: If the following apply to your dog, we encourage you to contact us. Our study team will review your dog’s medical history and test results to confirm eligibility.
L29: 
L30:   * ### Diagnosis
L31: 
L32: A pathology report has confirmed hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, or you are waiting for the result.
L33: 
L34:   * ### Recent spleen surgery
L35: 
L36: Your dog has had their spleen removed or has surgery scheduled.
L37: 
L38:   * ### Timing
L39: You are able to travel to the study site in Urbana Illinois within 21 days after surgery.
L40: 
L41:   * ### Previous treatment
L42: 
L43: Your dog has not received chemotherapy, radiation or another investigational drug.
L44: 
L45:   * ### Travel to Urbana, Illinois
L46: 
L47: You could bring your dog to Urbana for regular study visits.
L48: 
L49:   * ### Breeding
L50: 
L51: Your dog is not intended for breeding.
L52: 
L53: Wondering if your dog might qualify?
L54: Filling out the form doesn’t commit you to anything. Tell us a little about your dog, and if the study looks like a fit, we’ll connect you with the University of Illinois study team to confirm eligibility and answer your questions.
L55: 
L56: [Button: Contact the study team]
L57: 
L58: Ask about the study
L59: ## Tell us a little about your dog and how to reach you.
L60: 
L61: Asking about the study does not enroll your dog or commit you to taking part.
L62: 
L63: [Button: Contact the study team]
L64: 
L65: Questions about the study
L66: ## A cancer diagnosis brings a lot of decisions at once.
L67: 
L68: If your dog has been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma, this study could give them access to a new investigational treatment at no cost to you, with close care from the veterinary team at the University of Illinois.
L69: 
L70: [Button: Contact the study team]
L71: 
L72: Why might I consider this study for my dog?
L73: You may want to consider it if you and your veterinarian are looking at care options after hemangiosarcoma diagnosis and after spleen surgery. Your dog would receive the study drug and be monitored by the oncology team at Illinois, with study care paid for by Familiar. Taking part also helps researchers learn whether FAM-010 should be studied further for dogs with hemangiosarcoma. Our study team can help you understand how the study compares with other options for your dog.
L74: What would my dog and I need to do?
L75: 
L76: You would bring your dog to Urbana about every three weeks for treatment and health checks. The initial course is planned for six treatments over about three and a half months. Some dogs may receive up to twelve treatments. There are also follow-up calls and visits after treatment ends. Before you decide, our study team will explain the full schedule and what each visit involves.
L77: 
L78: Will my dog receive FAM-010?
L79: Yes. Every dog that joins this study receives FAM-010. There is no placebo. Dogs enter in small groups, and the dose may differ between groups as the team learns what dogs can tolerate.
L80: 
L81: Could FAM-010 improve survival for dogs with hemangiosarcoma?

L0@P0: Funded Study: Canine oral malignant melanoma
L1@P0: Study Title: Evaluating CD 45-binding interleukin-12 and interleukin-15 fusion peptide
L2@P0: in tumor bearing dogs.
L3@P0: Purpose of Study/Background/Objectives: We will be evaluating the safety and
L4@P0: immune activating effects of injecting the combination of IL-12/IL-15 fusion peptide into
L5@P0: oral melanoma tumors after one dose of radiation therapy. IL-12 and IL-15 have
L6@P0: separately been shown to work reasonably well to stimulate the immune system against
L7@P0: canine melanoma and safety has been proven in mice. Previous trials in pet dogs with
L8@P0: IL-12 have been successful. In this trial, canine patients with oral melanoma will be
L9@P0: evaluated to determine if administration of the IL12/IL-15 fusion protein can exert clinical
L10@P0: benefit.
L11@P0: Inclusion Criteria:
L12@P0: • Dogs at least 1 yr old and 8kgs
L13@P0: • Confirmed oral melanoma by cytology or histopathology
L14@P0: • Tumors must be 1-5 cm in diameter
L15@P0: • No previous radiation, chemotherapy or immunotherapy.
L16@P0: • While on study, no immunosuppressive/homeopathic/alternative therapy
L17@P0: including prednisone, cyclosporine or other immune modulatory agents.
L18@P0: • Adequate organ function for sedation and contrast
L19@P0: Exclusion Criteria
L20@P0: • Previous radiation, chemotherapy or immunotherapy
L21@P0: Eligibility Diagnostics: (Within 28 days of starting therapy)
L22@P0: • CBC, Chemistry panel, U/A
L23@P0: • Confirmation of oral melanoma by cytology or histopathology.
L24@P0: • Cytology of the draining lymph node
L25@P0: Treatment/Protocol:
L26@P0: Patients will receive 1 dose of radiation therapy and then 4 doses of IL-12/IL-15
L27@P0: intratumorally. Injections are given 2 weeks in a row, with a 3-week break, then 2
L28@P0: additional weeks of treatment. • At each treatment, blood samples will be collected over
L29@P0-1: 24hrs. Patients can either stay in hospital or return the next day for a blood draw. • After treatment, rechecks will be once every 4 weeks for 3 visits, then once every 8 weeks for
L30@P1: 3 visits, then every 12 weeks for a total of 1.5yrs, then study is complete. • We will use
L31@P1: complete bloodwork, lymph nodes samples, CT scans and biopsies of the tumor to track
L32@P1: patients’ response.

L23@P0: Patient Disease: Canine appendicular osteosarcoma.
L24@P0: Study Title: Investigating the immunological effects and safety of integrating stereotactic body

Canine soft tissue sarcoma amenable to surgical removal (https://vetmed.illinois.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/trial-Jen-101-alone-or-with-Hyla-for-STS.pdf)
【turn874792960view7】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Content type: application/pdf; Number of pages: 2; Source: open({"ref_id":"https://vetmed.illinois.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/trial-Jen-101-alone-or-with-Hyla-for-STS.pdf","lineno":null}); Total lines: 55
L0@P0: Funded Study: Canine soft tissue sarcoma amenable to surgical removal
L1@P0: Study Title: Evaluating the safety and immune activation properties of JEN101(anchored interleukin-12) following intratumoral injection in dogs with spontaneous
L2@P0: cancer
L3@P0: Purpose of Study/Background/Objectives: Stimulating the immune system to fight
L4@P0: cancer is a well-described and accepted treatment option for controlling cancer growth
L5@P0: and metastasis in people. Specific proteins known as cytokines are essential for
L6@P0: amplifying the immune response; however, certain cytokines—such as interleukin-12—
L7@P0: can be toxic when administered intravenously. Recent studies have demonstrated that
L8@P0: anchoring interleukins within tumor masses can effectively enhance anti-tumor activity
L9@P0: while minimizing systemic toxicity in both mouse and canine models. In a previous
L10@P0: study we showed that a similar immune strategy can be given safely in dogs with
L11@P0: naturally occurring tumors, specifically melanoma. The intent of this trial is to evaluate
L12@P0: dogs with surgically excisable soft tissue sarcomas to evaluate that there is an immune
L13@P0: response in the patients given JEN-101 intratumorally.
L14@P0: Inclusion Criteria:
L15@P0: • Dog with a confirmed diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma by either cytology or
L16@P0: histology.
L17@P0: • Tumors must be between 1-5 cm in diameter.
L18@P0: • Tumor must be amenable to marginal or complete surgical resection.
L19@P0: Exclusion Criteria:
L20@P0: • No previous radiation.
L21@P0: • Patients must have a 3-week washout from previous chemotherapy.
L22@P0: • While on study patients cannot have any
L23@P0: immunosuppressive/homeopathic/alternative therapy including prednisone,
L24@P0: cyclosporine or other immunomodulator agents.
L25@P0: Eligibility Diagnostics:
